---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to send and update messages, reply in threads, list channels and users, create channels, and fetch conversation history. Use whenever Gemini CLI needs to perform Slack operations — posting a message to a channel, resolving channel or user IDs, creating a channel, or reading message history — given a Slack bot token (SLACK_TOKEN).
---

# Slack API

## Overview

This skill wraps the Slack Web API in a dependency-free Node.js script (`scripts/slack_api.cjs`) that calls Slack directly and prints clean, LLM-friendly summaries plus JSON. No SDKs or config files — just a token.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+ (the script uses the global `fetch` API)
- A Slack token exported as `SLACK_TOKEN`:
  - **Bot token (`xoxb-…`)** for automation (recommended)
  - **User token (`xoxp-…`)** for user-scoped actions
- The Slack app must be installed in the target workspace with the scopes listed in [references/slack-api-reference.md](references/slack-api-reference.md)

## Quick Start

```bash
export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-your-token

# See all operations
node scripts/slack_api.cjs --help

# Post a message to #general (names and IDs both work)
node scripts/slack_api.cjs post-message general "Hello from Gemini CLI"

# Reply in a thread
node scripts/slack_api.cjs post-message C1234567890 "Reply text" --thread-ts 1715000000.000000

# List channels and users (for name -> ID resolution)
node scripts/slack_api.cjs list-channels --limit 100
node scripts/slack_api.cjs list-users --limit 100

# Create a private channel
node scripts/slack_api.cjs create-channel my-new-channel --private

# Read recent history
node scripts/slack_api.cjs get-history C1234567890 --limit 20
```

## Workflow

1. **Resolve identifiers first.** Most Slack APIs require IDs (`C…` channels, `U…` users), not names. Use `list-channels` and `list-users` to map names to IDs. The script accepts a channel name or ID for posting and history operations.
2. **Run the operation.** Export `SLACK_TOKEN`; the script reads it from the environment.
3. **Consume the output.** Every operation prints `Success: <summary>` followed by JSON (truncated to 8000 chars), or `Failure: <reason>` on stderr with exit code 1. If a listing has more pages, the output includes `next_cursor` — see [Pagination](references/slack-api-reference.md#pagination).

## Operations

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| `post-message <channel> <text>` | Send a message. `--thread-ts <ts>` replies in a thread; `--reply-broadcast` also posts to the channel |
| `update-message <channel> <ts> <text>` | Edit an existing message |
| `list-channels [--limit N] [--exclude-archived]` | List public and private channels with IDs |
| `list-users [--limit N]` | List workspace users with IDs and emails |
| `create-channel <name> [--private]` | Create a channel |
| `get-history <channel> [--limit N]` | Fetch recent messages from a channel |
| `get-thread <channel> <thread-ts> [--limit N]` | Fetch all replies in a thread |
| `channel-info <channel-id>` | Get channel metadata |
| `get-user <user-id>` | Get a user's profile |

## Message Formatting

Slack messages use `mrkdwn`: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `> quote`, `<https://example.com|link text>`, and `:emoji:`. Use `\n` for line breaks. See [Message Formatting](references/slack-api-reference.md#message-formatting) in the reference.

## Reference

For endpoint parameters, required OAuth scopes, pagination, rate limits, and error codes, read [references/slack-api-reference.md](references/slack-api-reference.md) when you need details beyond the basics above.

# Slack API Reference

## Table of Contents

- [Authentication & Tokens](#authentication--tokens)
- [OAuth Scopes](#oauth-scopes)
- [Endpoint Reference](#endpoint-reference)
- [Identifiers & Resolution](#identifiers--resolution)
- [Message Formatting](#message-formatting)
- [Threads](#threads)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
- [Error Handling](#error-handling)
- [Best Practices](#best-practices)

## Authentication & Tokens

- **Bot token (`xoxb-…`)**: represents the Slack app itself. Recommended for automation. Bot messages appear with the bot's name/icon.
- **User token (`xoxp-…`)**: represents a workspace user (obtained via OAuth with user scopes). Use only when acting as a specific user.
- Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request (the helper script does this automatically via `SLACK_TOKEN`).
- Keep tokens secret; never print them in full or commit them to source control.

## OAuth Scopes

Modern granular scopes required per operation. Note that installing the app with the legacy `bot` scope covers chat and channel basics.

| Scope | Needed for |
|---|---|
| `chat:write` | Post and update messages (`chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`) |
| `channels:read` | List/read public channels (`conversations.list`, `conversations.info`) |
| `groups:read` | List/read private channels |
| `channels:history` | Read public channel message history (`conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`) |
| `groups:history` | Read private channel history |
| `im:history` / `mpim:history` | Read DM / group DM history |
| `channels:manage` | Create public channels, invite members |
| `groups:write` | Create private channels |
| `users:read` | List users and get profiles (`users.list`, `users.info`) |
| `users:read.email` | Read user email addresses |

## Endpoint Reference

All endpoints return `{ "ok": true, ... }` on success or `{ "ok": false, "error": "<code>" }` on failure.

| Script op | Slack method | Key params | Scopes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `post-message` | `chat.postMessage` | `channel`, `text`, `thread_ts`, `reply_broadcast` | `chat:write` |
| `update-message` | `chat.update` | `channel`, `ts`, `text` | `chat:write` |
| `list-channels` | `conversations.list` | `types`, `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived` | `channels:read`, `groups:read` |
| `list-users` | `users.list` | `limit`, `cursor` | `users:read` |
| `create-channel` | `conversations.create` | `name`, `is_private` | `channels:manage` / `groups:write` |
| `get-history` | `conversations.history` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor` | `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` |
| `get-thread` | `conversations.replies` | `channel`, `ts`, `limit`, `cursor` | same as `get-history` |
| `channel-info` | `conversations.info` | `channel` | `channels:read`, `groups:read` |
| `get-user` | `users.info` | `user` | `users:read` |

Additional methods you may need that the script does not wrap: `conversations.invite` (add a bot/member to a channel), `conversations.leave`, `conversations.archive`, `chat.delete`, `reactions.add`, `users.lookupByEmail` (`email` param, scope `users:read.email`).

## Identifiers & Resolution

- **Channel IDs**: `C…` (public), `G…` (private or group DM), `D…` (DM).
- **User IDs**: `U…` (including bot users, which have `is_bot: true`).
- `chat.postMessage` accepts a channel **name** (with or without `#`) or an **ID**. Most other methods (history, info, replies) require an **ID**.
- To resolve a name to an ID: `list-channels` (then match on `name`), or `conversations.info`/`conversations.lookup` if you have an ID already.
- To resolve a user: `list-users` (match on `name`, `real_name`, or `profile.email`), or `users.lookupByEmail` with an email.
- Resolve once and cache; names can change but IDs are stable.

## Message Formatting

Messages use `mrkdwn`:

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, and fenced ```pre``` blocks
- `> quote` for blockquotes
- `<https://example.com|link text>` for hyperlinks
- `<@U123456>` to mention a user, `<#C123456>` to link a channel
- `:emoji_name:` for emoji
- Line breaks: `\n` in JSON, or literal newlines in the text

Limits: text is capped at 40,000 characters. When the script is invoked via the shell, quote the text argument and use `\n` escapes for newlines.

## Threads

- A thread is rooted at a message with `thread_ts` (same value as the message's `ts`).
- Reply in a thread by passing `thread_ts` to `chat.postMessage`.
- `reply_broadcast: true` also posts the reply to the channel itself (use sparingly).
- Fetch all replies with `conversations.replies` (`ts` = the root `thread_ts`).

## Pagination

- List/history methods return at most `limit` items (default 100) plus `response_metadata.next_cursor`.
- An empty `next_cursor` (or `""`) means there are no more pages.
- To fetch the next page, call again with `cursor=<next_cursor>`.
- Maximum limits: `conversations.list` 1000, `conversations.history` 1000, `users.list` 200.

## Rate Limits

- Slack enforces tiered rate limits per method (Tier 1 = 1+ request/sec per workspace; some methods are higher tiers).
- On throttling the API returns HTTP 429 (or `error: "ratelimited"`) with a `Retry-After` header — back off and retry after that delay.
- For bulk operations, add small sleeps between calls and reuse pagination instead of issuing many parallel requests.

## Error Handling

Common `error` codes from `data.error`:

| Code | Meaning / Fix |
|---|---|
| `invalid_auth` | Token is wrong or revoked. Check `SLACK_TOKEN`. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks the required OAuth scope for this method. See scopes table above. |
| `channel_not_found` | Channel ID/name does not exist or token cannot see it. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot is not a member. Invite it with `conversations.invite` or add it via the Slack UI. |
| `is_archived` | Channel is archived; unarchive before posting. |
| `name_taken` | Channel name already exists (creation failed). |
| `invalid_arguments` | Bad parameter, e.g. empty text or missing `ts`. |
| `message_not_found` / `thread_not_found` | The `ts` does not exist in that channel. |
| `user_not_found` | User ID does not exist. |
| `ratelimited` / `too_many_requests` | Throttled; back off per Retry-After. |
| `restricted_action` | Workspace admin policies block the action. |

## Best Practices

1. Use a bot token with the **minimum scopes** needed.
2. Resolve names to IDs once and reuse them.
3. Summarize history rather than echoing it verbatim to the user.
4. Truncate long output (the helper caps at 8000 chars).
5. Respect pagination and rate limits for large workspaces.
6. Never log or expose tokens.
